description: Machine-readable map from C++ Nullkiller2 policy sources to the Lua Nullkiller2 parity port.

entries.notes: Lua turn loop now normalizes vector snapshots into hero/object lookup indexes, including C++ host-exported visible visitable objects under nearbyObjects/visitableObjects, resets state, runs priority-pass behaviors, decomposes regular behaviors by tier, executes accepted tasks through the host command journal, handles task failures, trades resources, reserves town defenders, invokes pass-level artifact optimization, and ends turn. Native path/threat/analyzer snapshot parity remains incomplete.
Task plan merge/filter API and failure-action values are mirrored in Lua.
Parallel priority evaluation is intentionally serial in Lua; evaluator logic remains Lua-owned and deterministic.
Shipyard equivalence uses host object snapshots when available; otherwise it falls back to normal goal equality.
State and enum shell only.
Lua owns the persistent object-id sets and callback resolution helpers. Teleport-channel and subterranean-gate memory are placeholders until event snapshots carry enough teleport metadata.
Accepts host-provided difficulty settings and applies C++ constructor defaults.
Settings fields and all C++ getter names are mirrored while preserving direct table access for snapshot input.

Priority tiers, HeroRole, EvaluationContext defaults, embedded RewardEvaluator instance, non-critical strategical value clamp, and formula helpers are ported. RewardEvaluator resource/gold helper coverage lives in Engine/RewardEvaluator.lua; full object inspection remains pending.

Priority-tier scoring formulas and context builders are ported against Lua EvaluationContext/path/object snapshots, including ExecuteHeroChain, hero exchange, army upgrade, exploration point, adventure spell movement, stay-at-town mana recovery, defend-town, cluster unlock, exchange/swap-town defence, dismiss hero, and deterministic build-structure fields.

Deterministic resource pressure, army-cost, army reward/growth/cost, gold reward, artifact potential scoring, upgrade reward, strategic value, conquest value, town growth, mana recovery, witch-hut skill, skill-reward, and enemy-danger helpers are ported with fixture coverage and object-style calls through EvaluationContext.evaluator. Full live Rewardable inspection remains pending on richer snapshots.

Default fields, enum values, setter chaining, task conversion guard, helper exceptions, and base string formatting are mirrored. Engine-backed translated names are represented by host-snapshot fields until richer C++ input snapshots exist.
String output for generic goals is mirrored using deterministic Lua-side IDs and names from input snapshots.
Lua derives concrete goal classes from mirrored CGoal and ElementarGoal base tables.
Currently aggregates the ported initial goal subset.
Constructor, equality, and string policy are ported. Action execution still needs the Lua command/journal host path before full accept parity.
Action execution is intentionally a host command call and must be completed with validated command snapshots.
Constructor, equality, string policy, free-slot helper, purchase ordering, affordability capping, and stack-dismissal selection from upper-army slot snapshots are ported.

Lua accept emits granular upgrade/recruit/dismiss creature commands from town purchase, upgrade-info, and upper-army stack snapshots, and requests post-recruit visiting-hero movement when the town has no garrison hero.
Constructor, equality, hash, and string policy are ported. Decomposition needs CaptureObjectsBehavior parity.
Lua decompose delegates to a Lua capture-object behavior hook when present; native behavior is not called.
Lua accept uses return values instead of C++ fulfilled exceptions, while preserving the same task order.
Commented-out C++ decomposition remains non-active upstream and is not ported as executable policy.
Constructor, equality, string policy, and snapshot field expectations for boat cost/status/relation are ported.
Lua accept checks affordability, enemy ownership, and shipyard readiness before emitting the host build-boat command. Live shipyard snapshot coverage remains pending.
Constructor, equality, getHero, string policy, strongest-available selection, and host command intent are ported.
Cluster refresh side effects need explicit Lua state plumbing before this can be marked fully ported.
Constructor, spell access, equality, string policy, basic cast preconditions, target-object state, and host command intent are ported.

Town Portal selected-object state, occupied-town swap/error policy, caster ungarrisoning, cast command, and post-cast town movement are ported. Spell-mechanics target validation still requires host snapshots/helpers.
Lua accept locks resources through the Lua Nullkiller state/host shim and returns a fulfilled marker instead of throwing a C++ exception.
Lua accept emits the dismiss-hero host command intent and keeps the same invalid-hero guard.
Constructor, affected object policy, equality, string policy, and host-backed lock/unlock command sequencing are ported.

Lua accept emits granular swap, move-to-town, upgrade-creature, merge-stack, recruit-creature, cross-army merge/swap transfer, scout last-stack split, dismiss-creature, lock, and unlock commands. buildArmyIn extraction now sequences moveCreaturesToHero from Lua snapshots. Remaining exchange parity work is richer garrison/hero-exchange edge coverage and validator breadth.
Constructor state, equality, exchange count, affected-object policy, active/target state setup, object-cluster reset, and command intent are ported.

Path execution sets active hero/tile, target object, resets object clusters, invokes Lua-owned siege formation for immediate enemy town attacks, replays path nodes in native backward order through a granular moveHeroToTile host boundary, fail-closes blocked special actions with hero lock/pathfinder invalidation, executes composite, Dimension Door, adventure-spell, Build Boat, Whirlpool, Battle, Quest, BuyArmyAction, and explicit command special-action descriptors through Lua-owned primitive commands, recovers stale Dimension Door plans with hero lock/pathfinder invalidation, applies object-graph shortcutting against neutral live path-info fields, and rejects stale zero-turn live path snapshots before movement. Live host validation remains pending.
Constructor state, cluster/path accessors, equality, and string policy are ported.
Constructor state, equality behavior, and string policy are ported.
Constructor state and reinforcement-strength helper are ported against army-manager/path snapshots.
Both constructors, value getters, equality behavior, and string policy are ported.
Both constructors, getters, equality behavior, and string policy are ported.
Candidate evaluation, tile score, identity, string, and host movement intent are ported. Target discovery uses Lua/host candidate snapshots until ExplorationHelper is ported.
Path and discovery calculations require Lua snapshots from pathfinder/exploration helper ports.
Lua accept locks the hero through Lua state or host command intent.
Behavior identity and task-generation formula are ported against Lua snapshots.
ArmyManager and threat data are host/Lua snapshot inputs; task selection and city-hall gold-pressure guard are Lua-owned.
Lua exposes the mirrored SlotInfo shape, army-transfer selection helpers, reinforcement value helpers used by BuyArmyBehavior, total-army aggregation, and upgrade calculation.

Sorted-slot consolidation, faction/morale best-army filtering, scout-unit choice, scout last-stack retention, dwelling purchase selection, reinforcement purchase value, reinforcement transfer value, stack-power evaluation, total-army aggregation, and hill-fort/dwelling upgrade calculation are Lua-owned against snapshot fields.

Lua owns the secondary-skill evaluator and role-map update used by hero level-up choice. The role map is recomputed from visible hero/town snapshots with the native town-count cap and patrolling-main rule. Full bonus-derived speciality scoring still needs richer hero bonus snapshots.

Score maps, role-map update ordering, patrolling-main handling, bigger-map main-hero cap, and level-up secondary skill rules are mirrored in Lua from snapshots. Fighting-strength ranking uses exported primary skills, secondary skills, and optional speciality/evaluateHero fixture fields; exact native speciality bonus scoring remains pending on richer bonus snapshots.
Core static decision helpers and behavior shape are ported.
Hero/town/threat values are Lua snapshot inputs. Defensive emergency composition generation is Lua-owned.
Behavior identity and equality are ported.
Emergency fortification, gold-pressure filtering, missing-resource composition, and locked-resource skipping are Lua-owned against build analyzer snapshots.
Behavior identity and equality are ported.
Town/path filtering and composition creation are Lua-owned; path calculation is a snapshot/helper input.
Behavior identity and equality are ported.
Startup tavern build, nearest-hero chain, recruit allowance, startup swaps, fallback recruit, and garrison unlock task generation are Lua-owned against snapshots.
Candidate model, evaluator, behavior identity, and equality are ported.
Immediate-threat detection and best escape-path selection are Lua-owned; full tile path enumeration is supplied as snapshot/helper input.
Constructor modes, filters, equality quirk, and public visit-goal helper are ported.
Object filtering, should-visit decisions, safe path selection, blocked-action composition, and closest-way ratio are Lua-owned against path/object snapshots.
Behavior identity and equality are ported.
Main-hero delivery filtering, reinforcement thresholds, garrison exchange composition, upgrade thresholds, and visit-goal composition are Lua-owned against path/army-manager snapshots.
Behavior identity and equality are ported.

Town defence estimates, reserve/lock formulas, buy-army tasking, emergency defender movement, simplified recruit/counterattack hooks, and defensive priority assignment are Lua-owned against threat/path snapshots.
Behavior identity and equality are ported.
Locked-cluster traversal, blocker path trimming, unlock task composition, and capture-task pairing are Lua-owned against cluster/path snapshots.
Whirlpool and siege formation helper API is mirrored in Lua.
Lua owns one-creature decoy splits and citadel/castle siege slot sorting, using neutral creature aiValue/flying snapshot fields and primitive splitStack/swapCreatures host commands.
Dimension Door evaluator and composition policy are ported. Full tile scanning is represented by Lua/host exploration helper snapshots.

Hero-specific artifact relevance and equipped-artifact score formulas are Lua-owned against hero slot, stack bonus, spellbook, and artifact bonus snapshots. C++ host snapshots export hero artifactsWorn/artifactsInBackpack with instance IDs, possible slots, exported bonuses, constituents, and per-holder canBePutAt slot tables. GatewayPolicy has first-pass artifact equip/swap sequencing, including displaced-artifact backpack fallback when a direct swap is illegal; broader AIUtility helper coverage, cross-hero legality breadth, and full combined-artifact legality data remain pending.
Ordering and composition logic are Lua-owned; map iteration, path accessibility, fog counting, and spell target scanning still need full Lua ports or neutral snapshot helpers.
Boat evaluator, behavior identity, and equality are ported.
Special exploration objects, helper scan ordering, Dimension Door competition, scan-depth fallback, and neighbour exploration task creation are Lua-owned against object/helper snapshots.
Lua accepts both C++ resource ids (0..6) and Lua vectors (1..7). Market and callback access are host snapshot calls; trade choice logic is Lua-owned.

Dialog choice, teleport selection/probing, garrison-use, map-object selection, retreat, hero-exchange direction, battle/blocking/hero-created state events, move/reveal/hide/visit/object memory events, owner-change memory events, updateHitmapOnTileReveal tile-owner reset marking, lightweight artifact/resource/hero-stat/garrison/build/request/UI-window state callbacks, upgrade choice, dwelling recruitment, army-transfer, level-up skill choice with Lua role-map update, and first-pass artifact equip/swap policies are Lua-owned against snapshots. Creature upgrade policy consumes callback-exported UpgradeInfo snapshots for town and hero armed instances; the C++ host supplies raw upgrade candidates/costs and only executes resulting upgradeCreature commands. Turn snapshots now include visible visitable object records for behavior inputs. Artifact replacement uses exported hero artifact snapshots, per-holder canBePutAt tables, and the displaced-artifact backpack fallback when a direct swap is illegal. The availableArtifactsChanged, availableCreaturesChanged, advmapSpellCast, artifactAssembled, artifactDisassembled, artifactMoved, artifactPut, artifactRemoved, battleEnd, battleEnded, battleResultsApplied, battleStart, beforeObjectPropertyChanged, buildChanged, commanderGotLevel, garrisonsChanged, heroBonusChanged, heroCreated, heroExperienceChanged, heroGotLevel, heroExchangeStarted, heroInGarrisonChange, heroManaPointsChanged, heroMoved, heroMovePointsChanged, heroPrimarySkillChanged, heroSecondarySkillChanged, heroVisit, heroVisitsTown, newObject, objectPropertyChanged, objectRemoved, playerBlocked, playerBonusChanged, receivedResource, requestRealized, tileHidden, tileRevealed, showBlockingDialog, showGarrisonDialog, showRecruitmentDialog, showTeleportDialog, showTavernWindow, showMarketWindow, showUniversityWindow, showMapObjectSelectDialog, showThievesGuildWindow, showShipyardDialog, showHillFortWindow, and showInfoDialog callbacks are wired through Lua entry points. Query callbacks answer pending queries through HostCommands.answerQuery. makeSurrenderRetreatDecision is wired through a Lua return decision converted to BattleAction at the host boundary. Full hero speciality bonus snapshots, path/threat snapshots, teleport destination/probing memory, danger-aware blocking-dialog parity, cross-hero artifact legality breadth, full combined-artifact legality data, multi-step modded upgrade-chain differential breadth, and validator breadth remain pending.

Lua-side command boundary and journal used by goal accept methods and differential tests. C++ host execution is command-by-command, including granular hero movement, creature upgrades, stack merge/swap, stack split, and artifact swap commands. The audit checks that integer payload fields consumed by CLuaNullkiller2AI are extracted by LuaNullkiller2Runner. Host execution must not delegate to native policy.

JSON replay fixtures under tests/fixtures/replay exercise Lua entry points without a full game and compare normalized status, command journals, trace, and memory, including runDay hero-chain special-action command journals. Failures write actual JSON plus a first-difference summary under tests/fixtures/discrepancies. Native trace comparison is scaffolded separately; broad native trace export and lockstep comparison remain pending.

Native trace export is opt-in through VCMI_NK2_NATIVE_TRACE and currently emits comparator-compatible showMapObjectSelectDialog and makeSurrenderRetreatDecision records with decision-specific compare fields. The Lua comparator consumes the same schema and writes discrepancy artifacts. More native decision hooks and lockstep trace export remain pending.
Lua entry points used by the host runner for day turns and narrow callback policies.
